A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConDA research work. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the main text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and appendices A-C, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation and experimental outcomes, including interpolation, forecasting, classification, and neural-trajectory evaluations in Tables 1-4, Figure 5, and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical evaluations, revises forecasting results, and adds condition-interpolation and locality-test outcomes in Tables 12-13.

M1.justification: The diffusion inversion, InfoNCE embedding, spline/TEX/KDE traversal, and kNN lifting pipeline remains unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1-2. The new appendix experiments test existing components without revising the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The five original domains remain covered. Table 13 adds a limited text-to-image locality-test scenario using Stable Diffusion, although its dataset and prompts are unspecified. The other added evaluations use the retained fluid, calcium-imaging, and DISFA data.

E2.justification: Table 12 adds condition-only interpolation as a comparator against ConDA spline interpolation. Table 13 introduces Stable Diffusion as a locality comparator. Comparator membership in the existing main-text and appendix comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols hold the diffusion latent fixed while interpolating conditioning variables and perturb ConDA embeddings with scaled Gaussian noise. Table 13 reports edit distances from 0 to 3 for ConDA and 0 to 0.5 for Stable Diffusion. Existing forecasting splits, horizons, training settings, and metrics remain stated identically.

E4.justification: New Sections C.7-C.8 add substantive tests of two central questions: whether conditioning alone provides comparable control, and how reconstruction behaves as edits move farther through embedding space. These controls across three imaging domains substantially extend the retained solver, decoder, dimensionality, and orthogonality analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report plus/minus values for image-quality metrics, and the new tables follow that convention. v3 adds no run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures. Revised plus/minus magnitudes are changes to results.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises forecasting values and rankings across all three datasets under unchanged reported settings. DISFA spline PSNR changes from 36.31 to 37.17 and RMSE from 1.40 to 0.52, overtaking TEX-2; fluid TEX-2 RMSE instead worsens from 1.48 to 1.68. Tables 12-13 add condition-only and perturbation-response results, while Table 12 reuses existing ConDA spline scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, assumptions, equations, and appendix derivations are retained. The added Gaussian-perturbation and edit-distance expressions specify the locality experiment without introducing new theoretical results or revising mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about contrastive latent organization, separating editing from rendering, nonlinear traversal, solver independence, and validation across five domains. The new controls provide supporting evidence for existing claims.

C2.justification: C.7 interprets weaker condition-only reconstruction as inadequate control-space structure. C.8 links gradual degradation under larger edits to local kNN lifting, extending the retained locality limitation. Its strict monotonic-RMSE claim overstates Table 13: calcium RMSE decreases from 14.53 to 14.51 between distances 1.8 and 2.4.

D1.justification: v3 replaces future code-release wording and an anonymized flow-dataset placeholder with specific ConDA repository, Hugging Face dataset, and simulation-code locations. v2's explicit MIT-license commitment is omitted. Existing implementation details, hardware, and training settings remain unchanged; external resource availability was not checked.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. The Rex reference changes title and year while retaining the same arXiv identifier, and other reference edits correct capitalization or bibliographic details rather than introduce different literature.

P1.justification: The core narrative remains largely verbatim. v3 adds funding acknowledgments and supplementary-video descriptions, moves and rewrites the access statement before the references, adds correspondence and conference information, and edits bibliography wording.

P2.justification: v3 adds appendix Tables 12-13 and relocates the unchanged orthogonality table as Table 14. Existing Figures 1-14 are retained, with some repositioning and text reflow. Table 2's numerical revisions leave its display structure unchanged.

improvement.justification: The condition-only control strengthens evidence for ConDA's contribution, and the locality test quantifies a previously discussed limitation. Concrete code and dataset locations also improve reproducibility documentation. These gains are limited by the unspecified Stable Diffusion setup, unexplained Table 2 revisions, and the monotonicity claim that slightly overstates Table 13.
